==English==
{{wp}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{alter|en|connexion||dated}}
* {{alter|en|connex.||abbreviation}}

===Etymology===
{{ety|en|:der|enm:connexioun|tree=+}}
From {{inh|en|enm|conneccioun}}, {{m|enm|connexioun}}, {{m|enm|conneccyon}}, {{m|enm|conneccion}}, from {{der|en|la|connexionem}} (nominative {{m|la|connexio||a [[conclusion]], [[binding]] [[together]]}}), from {{m|la|connectō}}, an alternative spelling of {{m|la|cōnectō||to [[bind]] [[together]]}}, from compound of {{m|la|co-||[[together]]}} and {{m|la|nectō||to [[bind]]}}.

In [[American English]] mid-18c., spelling shifted from {{m|en|connexion}} to ''connection'' (equivalent to {{suffix|en|connect|ion}}), thus making {{m|en|connexion}} British dated and ''connection'' in international use.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/kəˈnɛkʃən/|[kʰəˈnɛkʃən]|~|[kʰəˈnɛkʃn̩]}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-connection.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɛkʃən|s=3}}
* {{hyph|en|con|nec|tion}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{lb|en|uncountable}} The act of [[connect]]ing.
#* {{quote-book|en|date=2005-10-02|author=Mieke Schüller|title=Howards End by E. M. Forster: "Only Connect!"|publisher=GRIN Verlag|isbn=9783638423182|page=2
|text=Forster employs personal relations to emphasize the importance of '''connection''' and mutual understanding}}
## [[coherence|Coherence]]; lack of [[disjointedness]].
## {{label|en|euphemistic}} [[sexual intercourse|Sexual intercourse]].
# The point at which two or more things are connected.
#: {{ux|en|the leak formed at the '''connection''' of the pipe and the boiler}}
## {{lb|en|transport}} A [[transfer]] from one transportation vehicle to another in scheduled transportation service.
##: {{ux|en|The bus was late so he missed his '''connection''' at Penn Station and had to wait six hours for the next train.}}
# A physical link between two things or places.
#: {{ux|en|the [[isthmus]] of [[Panama]] is the '''connection''' between North and South America}}
## An [[established]] [[communications]] or [[transportation]] link.
##: {{ux|en|computers linked by a network '''connection'''}}
##: {{ux|en|I was talking to him, but there was lightning and we lost the '''connection'''.}}
# A [[relationship]] or [[association]].
## A [[causal]] [[relationship]] between two [[phenomena]]; [[cause and effect]].
##: {{ux|en|the '''connection''' between overeating and obesity}}
##: {{ux|en|My headache has no '''connection''' with me going out last night.}}
## A [[relationship]] between people or groups of people.
##: {{syn|en|communion|q1=formal}}
##: {{ux|en|He parlayed his family '''connections''' into a prestigious job.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|date=2020-06-30|author=Tikiri Herath|title=The Girl Who Knew Their Names: A vigilante crime suspense novel|publisher=REBEL DIVA PRESS|isbn=9781989232767
|text=These two seemed to have a closer relationship than I knew. What's their '''connection'''?}}
## A feeling of [[mutual]] [[understanding]] and [[ease]] of [[communication]] between two or more people.
##: {{ux|en|As we were the only people in the room to laugh at the joke, I felt a '''connection''' between us.}}
## A [[contextual]] [[relationship]]; the [[commonality]] between two or more things.
##: {{usex|en|[[in this connection|in this '''connection''']]}}
# A person or persons related to oneself, through either [[family]] or [[business]].
#: {{ux|en|I have some '''connections''' in Lancashire.}}
#* {{RQ:Bramah Eyes of Max Carrados|passage=I hadn't much chance of buying a practice or dropping into a partnership worth having and I jibbed at setting up in some God-forsaken backwater and slipping into middle age 'building up a '''connection'''.'}}
## {{lb|en|usually|in the plural}} An [[acquaintance]] who is [[useful]] in a particular [[scenario]], especially in a [[corrupt]] or [[criminal]] way.
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1934|author=A. I. Voinova|title=Semi-precious Stones
|text=I have '''connections''' in the local committee. I shall bring them to bear, as long as the Council does not find fault!}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=2005|author=Roger R. Reese|title=Red Commanders: A Social History of the Soviet Army Officer Corps, 1918-1991|page=223
|text=General Zhigailo also used his '''connections''' to have an officer at the academy expelled from the party because he had criticized the general's behavior.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|date=2015-09-19|author= Linda J. Alexander |title=A Maverick Life: The Jack Kelly Story|publisher=BearManor Media
|text="I don't think Merv had ever been in the Mob," she added, but "he had '''connections'''." She recalled one of his '''connections'''.}}
## {{senseid|en|dealer}} {{lb|en|slang}} A [[drug dealer]].
##* {{RQ:Kerouac On the Road|passage=Now the final study was the drug habit. He was now in New Orleans, slipping along the streets with shady characters and haunting '''connection''' bars.}}
# {{lb|en|mathematics}} A [[set]] of sets that contains the [[empty set]], all one-element sets for any element that is included in any of the sets, and the [[union]] of any group of sets that are elements where the intersections of those sets is non-empty.
# {{label|en|religion}} {{alternative spelling of|en|connexion}}; a [[Methodist]] denomination as a whole, as opposed to its [[constituent]] [[church]]es, [[circuit]]s, [[district]]s and [[conference]]s.
